title: Divide Whole Numbers by Fractions
objective: I can explain what dividing a whole number by a fraction means (how many pieces fit, or how much is in one whole), find the quotient with a model or by multiplying by the reciprocal, and check it by multiplying.
model: bar model of whole bars cut into equal pieces of the divisor, counting how many groups fit (then the reciprocal shortcut)

widgets.component: prerequisite check: whole number as a fraction, fourths in 1 whole, 6 × 2/3, 1/4 of 12
widgets.root: Verified keys (5/1, 4, 4, 3). Only fraction-times-whole and unit-fraction counting, both earlier skills; nothing from this lesson is assumed.

widgets.component: whole number ÷ unit fraction, four numeric items
widgets.root: Recomputed 6÷1/3=18, 3÷1/5=15, 10÷1/4=40, 5÷1/2=10 against keys; distractors are the real errors (divide by the denominator, add, keep the quotient small).

widgets.component: tap-the-step: forgot to flip (4 ÷ 1/5) and flipped the dividend (8 ÷ 3/4)
widgets.root: Both steps are keyed to the faulty line (e=1) and the fixes recompute 20 and 10 2/3; they trap the two named misconceptions of keep-change-flip.

widgets.component: match six division expressions to five quotients
widgets.root: Computed 12,14,30,16,36,30; 5 ÷ 1/6 and 6 ÷ 1/5 share 30 so a student cannot match by size alone.

widgets.component: 6 ÷ 2/3 and two 'how much is in one whole' word problems
widgets.root: 6÷2/3=9; 6÷3/4=8; 5÷1/3=15 all match keys. 3.4 and 3.5 cover the lesson's second meaning (a part is given, find the whole) and say so in the stem.

widgets.component: generated whole ÷ fraction items: bare computation, whole-jar word problem, range estimation
widgets.root: Sampled L1-L3; the independent check() in tools/studio-gen.test.mjs agrees with the key; hints use keep-change-flip, which this lesson's vocabulary lists.

widgets.component: manipulable bar-cutting widget: cut each bar into d equal pieces, tap-count groups, type the quotient
widgets.root: This is the lesson's model made manipulable. Read assets/studio-act/barcut.js: grade() returns named feedback for multiplied, flipped, counted pieces, and leftover; the cut-count must make the divisor a whole number of pieces.

widgets.component: mastery check: 10 ÷ 1/4, reciprocal of 1/4, 9 ÷ 1/3, seed-tray word problem (16), what question 8 ÷ 1/4 asks
widgets.root: Keys recomputed (40, 4, 27, 16, 'how many 1/4-size pieces fit into 8'). The distractor −1/4 in 5.2 puts a negative number in front of students before 7-1, which is harmless but unnecessary.

widgets.component: 'A student answered 2.5. What did they do wrong?' with no problem stated
widgets.root: Root cause (all lessons): the practice-studio builder keeps each exit-ticket/connect.check follow-up question but drops the shared `scenario` that the questions depend on, so the stem reaches the student with no givens. Fix once in the builder (scripts/generate-practice-studios.mjs mastery assembly): prefix every follow-up stem with the scenario, or render the scenario as a passage above the item. Item 5.3 never says which division produced 2.5 (the scenario is 10 feet of rope cut into 1/4-foot markers), so the choices 'divided by 4 instead of by 1/4' cannot be judged.
widgets.replacement: Stem: 'A detective cuts a 10-foot rope into 1/4-foot evidence markers. A student wrote 2.5 markers for 10 ÷ 1/4. What did the student do wrong?' Keep the four choices; key stays 'They divided by 4 instead of by 1/4'.

widgets.component: word problem, range estimation, and missing-divisor reverse problem (2 ÷ ☐ = 3 1/5 → 5/8)
widgets.root: L4 reverse item checked: 2 ÷ 3 1/5 = 5/8; hint states dividend = quotient × divisor, which is the lesson's check-by-multiplying idea.

widgets.component: four tap-the-step error analyses (no flip, no flip, flipped the dividend, divided by the numerator only)
widgets.root: e indices point at the faulty line in each; the fixes recompute 9, 32, 4 4/5, 9.
Both ask for the reasoning the objective names (how many fit, why it exceeds the whole).
Recomputed 8÷2/5=20 (tape shows 2 reserve + 8 to pour = 10), 30−6=24, 5÷2/3 leaves 1/3, 14÷7/9=18, 5÷3/8=13 full jugs.

widgets.component: 9 liters fill 3/5 of the trench; find the whole
widgets.root: Bar figure is 3 of 5 parts shaded, matching 9 ÷ 3/5 = 15.

widgets.component: bar-cutting widget at leftover and reverse (pick the sentence) levels
widgets.root: Same verified widget; L3 forces a fractional quotient, L4 asks the student to name the division the model shows.
Six cards sorted correctly (for example, 4 liters into 1/3-liter cups divides; 3/4 of a 4-liter can multiplies); separates the lesson's operation from fraction-of.

widgets.component: 'dividing always makes smaller' misconception, greatest quotient, check by multiplying, write the expression
